author: Aryn Yklas
unitBoundaryScope: Generic errno classification, fixed capability/error transport, missing metadata and target refusal only. Unit inputs do not install or qualify seccomp, effective host capability, LSM, tracefs ACL or PID isolation.
denyingLayer: unknown unless independently established by retained operator-controlled policy evidence; EPERM/EACCES alone do not identify a layer
evidence: Wave 31 (lane 4, NativeA): .superpowers/sdd/approved-product/l4w31-evidence/NativeA/{permission-cases-sp-q-d12.txt,permission-cases-sp-q-k66.txt,oci-seccomp-probe.txt,oci-capability-probe-variants.txt,oci-container-smoke-*.txt}; scripts vm-permission-cases.sh, oci-*.sh. Kernels 6.1.0-54 (d12) and 6.6.162 (k66) are qualification kernels; the sp-oci rows (6.12.74, Docker 26.1.5) are case evidence only.

cases.name: seccomp-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable container denies perf_event_open with EPERM; retain PERFMON and approved target/tracefs visibility
cases.expected: CPU denied; denying layer unknown without external policy evidence; no samples or unconfined fallback
cases.observed: d12 and k66: a transient systemd unit with SystemCallFilter=~perf_event_open (EPERM) and all capabilities: cpu/off_cpu/runqueue_split denied, reason permission_denied, no samples. sp-oci (6.12): the audited profile with only perf_event_open set to EPERM: sandboxprobe reports EPERM for perf_event_open; the shipped profile itself lets the real helper capture 591 samples. The denying layer is named only because the filter was operator-supplied.

cases.name: host-capability-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable namespace lacks effective host PERFMON; host perf_event_paranoid remains unchanged
cases.expected: Real upstream perf scope decision reported; no assumption namespace capability grants host scope
cases.observed: d12 and k66 (paranoid 1): a user-namespace root with every capability only inside the userns, own-process target: cpu supported (the upstream paranoid decision for an own task), scheduler tracepoints denied (permission_denied, host tracefs). sp-oci (paranoid 3, Debian patch): no capabilities, PERFMON, and PERFMON+SYS_PTRACE+DAC_READ_SEARCH all give cpu denied; a privileged container is supported; the real helper in a PERFMON-only container is refused permission_denied. The extra capability the Debian kernel needs was not isolated.

cases.name: lsm-denied
cases.change: Operator-supplied disposable LSM policy denies perf_event_open while capability and seccomp allow it
cases.expected: Generic permission denial; retain independently supplied LSM evidence instead of inferring cause from EPERM
cases.observed: sp-oci: docker-default AppArmor profile (operator-supplied by the runtime) with PERFMON and the audited seccomp profile: helper refuses with permission_denied while the same container with AppArmor unconfined captures; the kernel audit log shows apparmor="DENIED" operation="ptrace" profile="docker-default" requested_mask="read". The LSM mediated ptrace-read of the target, not a perf_event_open hook (no LSM with that hook was loaded; d12/k66 have AppArmor loaded but no apparmor_parser).

cases.name: tracefs-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable mount namespace hides tracefs while self CPU perf remains permitted
cases.expected: CPU supported and off-CPU unavailable independently; not successful full qualification
cases.observed: d12 and k66: tmpfs over /sys/kernel/tracing in a private mount namespace: cpu supported, off_cpu and runqueue_split unsupported (tracefs_unavailable), scheduler_event_open unsupported.

cases.name: target-visibility-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable PID/mount namespace hides authorized target proc identity
cases.expected: Target refusal before acquisition; no hostPID escalation
cases.observed: d12 and k66: a new PID namespace with its own /proc and a host target PID: 'target identity unavailable', no acquisition attempted.

cases.name: hidepid-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable PID namespace remounts /proc with hidepid=2; a PERFMON-only account targets a process of another uid
cases.expected: Target refusal before acquisition; the caller cannot read the target's /proc entry
cases.observed: d12 and k66: with hidepid=0 the caller lists 6 pids and reads /proc/<pid>/stat; with hidepid=2 it lists 4 and cannot; both probe runs report 'target identity unavailable' (the foreign-uid target is refused at ns/pid in both, so the probe output alone does not separate the layers; the visibility change is the evidence).

cases.name: tracefs-dac-denied
cases.change: Helper-shaped account (uid 65534, only CAP_PERFMON, same-uid target) against root-owned 0700 tracefs; no ACL granted
cases.expected: CPU supported and off-CPU unavailable independently
cases.observed: d12 and k66: cpu supported, off_cpu and runqueue_split unsupported with reason tracefs_unavailable (the probe does not distinguish a DAC denial from a missing mount; the closed reason is tracefs_unavailable). Granting a tracefs ACL was not attempted: no setfacl on the VMs and an ACL grant would change host state.

deploymentPrerequisites.systemd: Use packaging/systemd/soundpost-perf-acquire.service only after dedicated UID, root-owned policy, proc/tracefs/cgroup access and PERFMON approval
deploymentPrerequisites.container: cap_drop ALL; cap_add PERFMON only after operator approval; audited deploy/seccomp/soundpost-perf.json; read-only approved proc/tracefs/cgroup views; read-only host /etc/machine-id; private Unix socket mount; no network exposure
deploymentPrerequisites.compose: Separate optional helper service with same container restrictions; exporter shares dedicated local UID and private runtime socket only, never tenant ingress identity
deploymentPrerequisites.kubernetes: Optional helper with drop ALL/add PERFMON, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, Localhost audited seccomp, read-only approved metadata mounts including /etc/machine-id; target PID visibility and every host mount require explicit authorization; Pod Security rejection remains denied
